text:
incident-bot: Pager fired — GPU vmem hotwave detected on pool prod-eu-2. Metric: gpu.vmem.used_pct >= 92% for 3m. Severity: P1. Suggested immediate actions: aggressive evictions, reroute low-priority traffic to fallback pools. Link: https://metrics.redwood.ai/alert/8367123456

Anika: acked. I'm on it. paging PD and starting mitigation.

pagerduty-bot: Incident 8345 opened, service: inference-prod, incident key: igp-8345. Assigned to: Anika. status: acknowledged.

Dmitri: seeing repeated `CUDA error: out of memory` in kvestimator containers. logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z kvestimator-7f8b9: [ERROR] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (0x702)
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z kvestimator-7f8b9: [WARN ] KV cache eviction triggered for model-7
```

Kai: quick mitigation: enable aggressive kvcache eviction policy on pool prod-eu-2 and reroute low-priority traffic to fallback-pool. I'll run the evict command.

Kai:
```
# set eviction to aggressive
./opsctl pool update prod-eu-2 --kv-evict=aggressive
# scale down batchers for model-7
./opsctl service scale inference/model-7 --replicas=2
```

Amber (SRE): noted customer hit — Ellen (CS) reporting increased 5xxs and timeouts. Ellen can you share which tenants?

Ellen (CS): we have two paying customers affected: "AcroData" and "LocaleAI". Approx 3% of requests failing and spikes in latency to 3.8s. Customers flagged via support tickets 8421/8422.

Anika: acknowledging handoff to Amber for customer comms. I'll keep working evictions + reroute. Can someone run a canary on fallback-pool?

Dmitri: starting canary now: routing 5% traffic for model-7 to dedicated-fallback pool.

pagerduty-bot: Incident escalated to team: sre-oncall, responder: Amber (SRE).

Amber (SRE): taking over oncall. ETA for node replacement if eviction doesn't stabilize: 25-35m. For now, continue evictions and canary traffic. I'll coordinate with infra to pre-stage replacement GPUs.

Kai: eviction ran, KV reclaim up 18GB on nodes in prod-eu-2. Observed drop in alloc failures. Monitoring.

Anika: saw immediate drop in OOM errors in logs, but latency still elevated for a subset. Increasing canary to 10% to validate fallback throughput.

Ellen (CS): notified AcroData and LocaleAI: standard incident notification sent, ETA 45m for resolution. Keeping them updated.

incident-bot: Pager update: 8367123456 — ack by Anika at 2026-03-15T09:13:10Z; status: mitigation in progress.

Amber (SRE): If stable for 10m, we'll keep replacement on standby and close the page. If errors persist, escalate to infra change window. I'll hand off to @Dmitri in 30m for follow-up.

Dmitri: logged followup ticket INFRA-1298 for GPU node reprovisioning if needed.

Kai: monitoring graphs: gpu.vmem.used_pct down to 78% cluster-wide after evictions; request error rate back to 0.4%.

Anika: thanks all. leaving notes in the incident doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/8367123456-hotwave

Amber (SRE): handoff to Dmitri in 30m. current status: mitigated (evictions + reroute). customer impact: degraded for 45m, limited tenants, CS notified. I'll mark pagerduty incident as 'in progress' and update severity after watch window.

Dmitri: acknowledged handoff. will monitor through 10pm UTC, ping if anything flares.

pagerduty-bot: Incident 8345 status changed: in_progress. playbook: gpu-memory-hotwave.

Anika: final note: root cause suspected to be sudden KV cache retention spike from a misbehaving batch job (diagnostics attached). Next steps: rollout kvcache retention guard and scheduled evictor cron. :white_check_mark:

Ellen (CS): closing support loop: customers informed, monitoring for additional tickets.

Amber (SRE): closing this Slack thread for handoff. continuing watch for 2 hours. :eyes:
